text: Here to be recognised rather than used: strength does not survive translation. A word glossed damn on this card can be unsayable in the language beside it, and a language's strongest word is often the one this section had to leave out.

Japanese does almost none of this with vocabulary. Contempt is carried by grammar instead -- a blunt second-person pronoun, the plain imperative, the abrupt verb endings -- so the anger sits in the ending rather than in a word you can look up. The rows above are close to the whole of the lexicon.
